metadata.method: Official product pages/datasheets take precedence. No sparse number is used as dense. Deterministic arithmetic from an official architectural throughput ratio is explicitly tagged derived. Null means no trustworthy public number was found.
metadata.rentalPolicy: Per-card public hourly offers only. Request-access pages, whole-server monthly quotes without a public price, and compute-provider payouts are not treated as rental prices.

candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.name: Intel Gaudi 3
candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.reason: Official whitepaper provides FP8 1678 TFLOPS, BF16 1678 TFLOPS, FP16/TF32 459 TFLOPS, 128GB HBM2e and 3.7TB/s, but does not publish a peak INT8 TOPS in the MME table. INT8 software ops are not evidence of threshold peak, so it is not admitted by the strict filter.

candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.name: Moore Threads MTT S5000
candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.reason: Official material gives 80GB, 1.6TB/s, FP8-through-FP64 support and roughly 1000 TFLOPS dense AI compute, but the precision of that peak and a distinct dense INT8 figure are not publicly pinned down.

candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.name: Tenstorrent Blackhole p100a/p150a/p150b
candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.reason: Official docs give 28/32GB, 448/512GB/s, 120 Tensix cores, BFP8 664 TFLOPS and native INT8, but no official dense INT8 peak. BFP8 is not used as INT8.

candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.name: Enflame S60
candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.reason: A 2024 independent accelerator card is identifiable, but detailed public numbers are mostly secondary and conflict; vendor/filing pages do not expose a sufficient exact dense INT8+memory spec set.

candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.name: Cambricon MLU590
candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.reason: Public sources conflict on memory capacity, bandwidth and INT8 peak; no stable official product table was found.

candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.name: MetaX C500/C550
candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.reason: Official filing confirms card identity, 64GB HBM2e, launch timing and interconnect, but exact compute/bandwidth figures available publicly are largely secondary. Keep out of the strict high-confidence set.

candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.name: Biren BR106B / BR166
candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.reason: Official product pages identify newer cards but do not expose sufficient exact memory, bandwidth and dense INT8 data for the filter.

candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.name: Iluvatar CoreX Tiangai 150
candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.reason: Vendor page exposes 64GB HBM and 350W only. A government procurement requirement names >=660 INT8, >=220 FP16 and >=1100GB/s for a BI-V150-64-01, but these are lower-bound tender requirements, not exact vendor peaks.

candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.name: Huawei Ascend 910B/910C
candidatesEvidenceInsufficient.reason: Chip/platform names are well known, but no official standalone add-in-card product page with a complete, unambiguous per-card peak/memory/bandwidth table was found. Atlas 300I A2 is included instead because it is a defined PCIe card.
